cards.text: Last time, David's kingdom got its gatekeepers and treasuries all lined up. Now it's the army's turn, friend, so grab a clipboard. Here comes the list of the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officers who served the king.

cards.question: David's army was split into divisions. How did those divisions serve the king?

answers.text: Each division took its own month
Every division served all year long
Each division served only in wartime

cards.question: Some of David's army divisions were much bigger than others.

cards.text: Then come the twelve divisions, one for each month, each with 24,000 men and a commander in charge. One name to spot is Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, mighty among the Thirty, who takes the third month. Twelve crews, and every crew knows its month. Friend, I can't even remember what day I last cleaned my oven.
Next comes a list of the leaders over the tribes of Israel, one name for each tribe. Over Judah is Elihu, one of David's brothers. That's one way to keep it in the family!
Then the list stops for something David did NOT do. He didn't count the men aged twenty or under.

cards.question: David left the men aged twenty or under out of the count. Why?

answers.text: The LORD said Israel would be as many as the stars
The LORD said only older men would go to battle
The army leaders said they already had plenty of men

cards.text: Then Joab son of Zeruiah gets to work and starts counting the men. Hold on to your apron, friend.

cards.question: Joab finished counting all the men.
Joab's census didn't go well. Because of it, ___ came upon Israel.
So what happened to the number Joab got from his count?

answers.text: It never went into King David's records
It was carved into the palace wall
It was read out loud to all Israel

cards.text: Next up are the officials in charge of King David's property: storehouses, fields, vineyards, olive and sycamore trees, olive oil, herds, camels, donkeys and flocks. Obil the Ishmaelite gets the camels. Friend, I'm in charge of ONE oven, and some days the oven is STILL winning.
Last, the people around the king himself. David's uncle Jonathan is a counselor, a man of insight and a scribe.

cards.question: Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended to the sons of the king.
Ahithophel was the king's counselor. Hushai the Archite had a title of his own. He was the king's ___.

cards.text: Ahithophel doesn't keep that counselor seat forever. First, Jehoiada son of Benaiah takes it after him.

cards.question: Who took Ahithophel's old counselor seat after Jehoiada son of Benaiah?

cards.text: And over the king's whole army? Joab. Army, tribes, property, counselors, David's got the whole kingdom on one chart. Meanwhile I've been hunting for my other oven mitt since Tuesday.

findings.problem: The opening card recaps the previous passage ("Last time, David's kingdom got its gatekeepers and treasuries all lined up"). The previous passage is context only, and recap cards are not allowed.
The card tells facts from 1 Chronicles 26 (gatekeepers, treasuries) but cites only 1 Chronicles 27:1. The previous passage is not part of the lesson.

rule.text: The passage right before it is also provided, for context only. It is not part of the lesson.

findings.problem: "Last time" assumes the baker did the previous lesson. Papa Dorin doesn't know the baker's history.

rule.text: **What he doesn't know:** anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before. In lessons, he's never told, because every baker gets the same lesson.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about the division sizes (24,000 each). That is a count from the census-style list of divisions, which is a long stretch.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: "One name for each tribe" isn't true to the text. The list includes Aaron, who is not a tribe, splits Manasseh into two halves, and has no leaders for Gad or Asher.

rule.text: **Noticing.** What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: "That's one way to keep it in the family!" suggests Elihu got the post because he was David's brother. The text gives no reason for his appointment.

rule.text: **Reasons.** He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "So what happened to the number" ties the number not being recorded to the wrath on card 10 as a result. Verse 24 joins the two only with "and".

rule.text: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Choice card on the list of the king's officials (vv. 32-34), a name list that doesn't move the passage. Card 14 also just restates the verse as a true/false with no setup.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Choice card on a detail from the name list of officials (Hushai's title).

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Choice card on who succeeded Ahithophel, a detail from the name list of officials.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Most choice cards can't be reasoned out from the earlier cards and are pure discovery or luck: card 2 (card 1 never mentions the monthly rotation), card 3, card 10, card 11, card 14, card 15 and card 17. Only cards 7 and 9 are informed guesses.

rule.text: **A few discovery questions are fine.** Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: This isn't a summary card for a long stretch, but it runs three to four sentences.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: Cards 13 and 16 are flat restatements with no Papa Dorin voice. The humor elsewhere (for example card 5) reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Almost the whole passage is long stretches: the division list (vv. 1-15), the tribal leaders (vv. 16-22), the property officials (vv. 25-31) and the counselors (vv. 32-34). Only vv. 23-24 move the passage. If long stretches get no choice cards, the stop can't have at least as many choice cards as story cards. The ratio rule pushes toward choice cards on list details instead.
findings.question: When a passage is almost entirely long stretches, which rule wins: "A long stretch never gets a choice card" or "Choice cards are equal to or more than story cards in every stop"? Can such a stop have fewer choice cards than story cards, or may choice cards ask about the purpose or structure of a list (like the monthly rotation in v. 1)?
